subject: Helm + Ansible alignment for SR-IOV & segmented VPC — private deployment IaC review
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: John Liu <john.liu@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Helm + Ansible alignment for SR-IOV & segmented VPC — private deployment IaC review

John — following up from yesterday's kickoff, attaching a short proposal that outlines the Terraform/Helm/Ansible split we think will meet Meridian's SR-IOV and VPC segmentation requirements. Key asks from our side:
- Confirm whether SR-IOV needs to be enabled on all GPU hosts or only on a prov folder (edge pool).
- Any existing NSX/T3 network policies we must avoid or mirror.

Attached: priv-deploy-iac-proposal.md (high-level split), helm-chart-diff.patch (what Helm will change), ansible-role-sriov.yml (Ansible role prototype).

Proposed timeline: internal review -> security checklist -> staging deploy (2 weeks). Can you share the infra team's preferred change window?

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: John Liu <john.liu@meridianhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: infra-team@meridianhealth.com
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 12:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helm + Ansible alignment for SR-IOV & segmented VPC — private deployment IaC review

Hi Naomi — thanks for the proposal and the attachments. A couple of clarifying questions from the Merid. infra side:
- We plan to enable SR-IOV only on the GPU host pool used for inference (not on control/infra nodes). Can your Ansible role scope by host labels?
- For VPC segmentation, we need explicit egress-only routes for PHI-handling subnets and a mapping to our audit flow. Does your Terraform output include route table IDs and a way to disable default internet egress?

Prefer a review window on Thursday afternoon (PST). Also please add a separate plain-text summary for our procurement/security reviewers — they want a one-page list of security controls changed by the deployment.

Thanks — John
John Liu
Senior Cloud Architect, Meridian HealthTech
john.liu@meridianhealth.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: John Liu <john.liu@meridianhealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 11:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helm + Ansible alignment for SR-IOV & segmented VPC — private deployment IaC review

John / team — quick technical response and attachments: helm-chart-diff.patch (same as Naomi's but annotated), ansible-role-sriov.yml (updated with host_label selectors), and a small Terraform snippet we will output as variables for route_table_ids. Highlights:
- Ansible role: we added host_label: gpu_inference=true and a conditional task to only enable SR-IOV on matching hosts. See ansible-role-sriov.yml (task: enable sriov if ansible_facts.linux and host_label true).
- Terraform: modules/network will export map(string) of route_table_ids per-segment. We'll add a boolean variable disable_default_egress that, when true, replaces the default route with NACLs + Egress-only NAT for PHI subnets.
- Helm: chart changes are minimal (nodeSelector + tolerations) — the helm patch includes a templated nodeSelector for gpu_inference. This keeps runtime config out of Terraform.

Security checklist (short):
1) SR-IOV changes limited to labeled hosts; no kernel changes on control plane.
2) Route tables explicit and auditable; Terraform state includes mapping IDs.
3) Audit hooks: we add a CloudTrail/Flow logs bucket policy for deposition of logs during rollout.

I'll plan to walk the Merid. team through the annotated patches on Thursday 2026-05-21 at 14:00 PST. Naomi — can you send a calendar invite and include the one-page security summary John requested?

--
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — short status and next steps after the walkthrough:
- Meeting outcome (2026-05-21 14:00 PST): Meridian confirmed SR-IOV only on gpu_inference host group; procurement/security accepted the security checklist pending a minor change to retention for Flow Logs.
- Actions assigned:
  * Mateo: add disable_default_egress variable and inject route_table_ids mapping into outputs (due 2026-05-24).
  * Dev: add automated checklist step in our CI that fails the PR if ansible-role-sriov.yml lacks host_label condition (due 2026-05-23).
  * Naomi: produce the one-page security summary for procurement and upload to the Drive link, include pointer to PRIVDEPLOY-438 (done).

Attached: updated ansible-role-sriov.yml (includes host_label guard), one-pager-security-summary.pdf (attachment stub).

Please confirm owners have the items noted and I'll open the staging rollout ticket after Mateo's change.

Best,
Naomi

Redwood Inference
